separable: separable — *nail down the details*, and *nail the details down*; a pronoun object must sit in the middle: *nail it down*, never ✗ *nail down it*
gloss: To settle the exact details of something so that they are final.
examples: We still need to *nail down* a date for the wedding.
They *nailed down* the last few terms of the contract on Friday.
She's *nailing* the schedule *down* this afternoon.

separable: separable — *nail down the cause*, *nail the cause down*, *nail it down*; never ✗ *nail down it*
gloss: To find out or state something exactly, leaving nothing vague.
examples: Investigators still haven't *nailed down* the cause of the fire.
The report never *nails down* who approved the payment.
Once we've *nailed* it *down*, I'll email the whole team.

ru: добиваться, добиться чёткого ответа (от кого-л.); припирать, припереть к стенке
separable: separable — *nail the contractor down to a price*; with a pronoun the person goes in the middle: *nail him down*, never ✗ *nail down him*
gloss: To get a firm answer or commitment out of someone who keeps avoiding one.
examples: I can't *nail* him *down* to a time.
The reporter finally *nailed* the senator *down* on the tax question.
Good luck *nailing* her *down* — she changes her mind daily.

separable: the object always comes in the middle, because *after* keeps its own object — *name a street after her*, *name him after his grandfather*; never ✗ *name after him a street*
gloss: To give a person or place the name of someone else, in that person's honor.
examples: They *named* the baby *after* her grandmother.
The park is *named after* a local firefighter.
We're *naming* him *after* my dad.
contrast: American English also says *named for*: *a street named for Dr. King*. British English keeps *named after*; both are correct in the US.

separable: separable — *narrow down the list*, *narrow the list down*, *narrow it down*; never ✗ *narrow down it*
gloss: To reduce a long list of possibilities to a small, workable number.
examples: We've *narrowed* the list *down* to three candidates.
Can you *narrow* it *down* a little?
Police are *narrowing down* the search area.

separable: no object at all — intransitive; you *nod off* during a movie, never ✗ *nod someone off*
gloss: To fall asleep without meaning to, usually while sitting up.
examples: He *nodded off* halfway through the movie.
I keep *nodding off* at my desk after lunch.
Grandpa *nods off* in his chair every afternoon.
contrast: The *d* doubles: *nod → nodded off, nodding off*, never ✗ *noded off*.

ru: рыться, порыться (в чужих вещах); вынюхивать, разнюхивать; совать нос
separable: inseparable — often with no object at all (*stop nosing around*), and when a place follows, *around* holds on to it: *nosing around my desk*, never ✗ *nosing my desk around*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*quit nosing around*), transitive (*nosing around my office*)
gloss: To search through someone's things or ask quiet questions in order to find out something private.
examples: I caught him *nosing around* my desk.
Reporters *nosed around* for weeks before the story broke.
Don't *nose around* in other people's mail.

ru: опережать, опередить (на волосок); обходить, обойти с минимальным перевесом
separable: separable — *nosed out the favorite*, *nosed the favorite out*, *nosed him out*; never ✗ *nosed out him*
gloss: To beat someone by a very small margin.
examples: The Tigers *nosed out* the Bears 21–20.
She *nosed* him *out* in the last fifty meters.
He's *nosing out* the favorite with two laps to go.

separable: separable — *note down the number*, *note the number down*, *note it down*; never ✗ *note down it*
gloss: To write something down quickly so that you will not forget it.
examples: *Note down* the reference number before you hang up.
She *noted down* everything the doctor said.
He was *noting* the license plate *down* as they drove off.
contrast: *write down* and *jot down* are far commoner in American speech; *note down* is correct but a shade more formal.

separable: separable — *offer up a suggestion*, *offer a suggestion up*, *offer it up*; never ✗ *offer up it*
gloss: To put something forward for other people to consider, use, or accept.
examples: He *offered up* his own room for the night.
Nobody was willing to *offer up* an explanation.
She's *offering up* a few ideas at tomorrow's meeting.

ru: открываться, открыться; раскрываться, раскрыться (рассказать о личном)
separable: no object — intransitive. The listener takes *to* and the subject takes *about*: *opened up to her about the divorce*; never ✗ *open up your feelings*
gloss: To start talking honestly about your feelings or your private life.
examples: It took months before he *opened up* about the accident.
She doesn't *open up* to many people.
He's slowly *opening up* in therapy.

separable: separable — *open up new markets*, *open new markets up*, *open them up*; never ✗ *open up them*
gloss: To create new possibilities, or make something available that was closed off before.
examples: The scholarship *opened up* a whole new career for her.
A second runway would *open up* the airport to bigger planes.
Streaming has *opened up* the music business to anyone with a laptop.

ru: появляться, появиться (о вакансии, месте); освобождаться, освободиться
separable: no object — intransitive: the job, seat or spot is the subject. *A position opened up*, never ✗ *they opened up a position* in this sense
gloss: (Of a job, place, or chance) to become available.
examples: A position *opened up* in the design team.
Let me know if anything *opens up*.
Two seats are *opening up* on the board next spring.

separable: separable when there is an object — *open up the store*, *open the store up*, *open it up*; just as often there is no object at all: *they open up at seven*
transitivity: both — transitive (*open up the shop*), intransitive (*the bakery opens up at six*)
gloss: To start a business, or to unlock a shop or office and begin the day's work.
examples: They're *opening up* a bakery on Third Street.
Whoever gets there first *opens up*.
He *opened* the store *up* an hour early.

separable: no object — intransitive, and usually an order shouted at a closed door: *Open up!* Name the door and you are back to the plain verb: *open the door*
gloss: To unlock and open a door for someone waiting outside.
examples: *Open up!* It's the police.
He banged on the door until somebody *opened up*.
Nobody was *opening up*, so we left a note.

ru: выбирать, выбрать; останавливать, остановить свой выбор на
separable: inseparable — *for* never lets go of its object: *opted for the cheaper plan*, *opted for it*; never ✗ *opted the cheaper plan for*
gloss: To choose one thing rather than another.
examples: Most buyers *opt for* the base model.
We *opted for* an early flight.
She's *opting for* a year off before college.
contrast: *opt* never stands alone: it needs *for*, *in*, *out*, or a *to*-infinitive — *opted to stay*.

separable: no object — intransitive; the thing you join takes *to* or *into*: *opt in to the plan*, *opt into the study*; never ✗ *opt it in*
gloss: To choose to take part in something you are not included in automatically.
examples: Employees have to *opt in* to the new savings plan.
About half the staff *opted in*.
You're *opting in* the moment you check that box.

ru: отказываться, отказаться (от участия); выходить, выйти (из программы)
separable: no object — intransitive, and what you are leaving takes *of*: *opt out of the trial*; never ✗ *opt the trial out*
gloss: To choose not to take part in something you would otherwise be included in.
examples: You can *opt out* of the mailing list at any time.
Almost nobody *opted out*.
Parents are *opting out* of the testing in large numbers.

separable: separable, and the person normally sits in the middle — *orders everyone around*, *don't order me around*; never ✗ *order around me*
gloss: To keep telling someone what to do in a bossy, unpleasant way.
examples: Stop *ordering* me *around*.
He *ordered* the interns *around* all summer.
She's tired of being *ordered around* by people half her age.

ru: заказывать, заказать еду на дом (с доставкой)
separable: normally no object — *let's order in*; when the food is named it goes after the particle: *ordered in pizza*, never ✗ *ordered pizza in*
transitivity: both — usually intransitive (*let's order in*), sometimes with the food named (*they ordered in Thai*)
gloss: To have restaurant food delivered to your home instead of cooking or going out.
examples: I'm too tired to cook — let's *order in*.
We *ordered in* pizza and watched the game.
They've been *ordering in* every night this week.

separable: no object — intransitive; what you admit takes *to*: *own up to the mistake*; never ✗ *own the mistake up*
gloss: To admit that you did something wrong.
examples: Nobody would *own up* to breaking the window.
He finally *owned up* the next morning.
She's *owning up* to her part in it.
